blurb:
No cover. No setlist. Just two pianists going at it for three hours while the crowd decides what gets played. Dueling Pianos at Park Bench in The Battery is the kind of Saturday night that starts as 'we'll just stay for one drink' and ends at midnight.

The show runs 8:30 to 11:30pm. General seating is first-come, first-served and it fills up, so if you're going with a group, reserving a table ahead of time is the smarter move. The Battery makes it easy to grab dinner somewhere first and walk over.

Free admission, good energy, and a crowd that's actually there to have fun. Hard to argue with that on a Saturday night in October.
scoring_notes: No-cover Saturday night entertainment at The Battery is very accessible for this demographic. Interactive format skews adult and social, fits young professionals well. Lower uniqueness score because Dueling Pianos is a recurring Saturday event, not a one-off. Still included because the entertainment value and zero cost are strong selling points for this audience.

blurb:
Fair Oaks Recreation Center is going all-in on Halloween Wednesday night with music, games, treats, hot cocoa, and costumes. It runs 6 to 8 PM, it's free, and it's built for the whole family.

If you've got kids who want one more Halloween event before the real thing hits Thursday, this is a clean, easy option. Costumes are highly encouraged, which is really the only rule worth following here.

Nothing complicated about this one. Show up in costume, grab some cocoa, let the kids run around. Sometimes that's exactly what the week calls for.
scoring_notes: Lower uniqueness since it's a fairly standard rec-center Halloween party. Skews toward younger families, which is a portion but not the dominant segment of this audience. Included because it's free, local, and falls squarely in the issue window. Good filler pick if the newsletter needs a family-friendly community event.

blurb:
Right in the neighborhood and right before Halloween, the Sewell Mill Library is throwing a free costume party Wednesday evening and it's one of the easier wins of the week for families with younger kids still at home.

Costumes are encouraged, activities are family-friendly, and it runs from 5 to 7 PM — early enough to be home and not blow up anyone's school night. Sewell Mill is literally in East Cobb, so you're not driving anywhere. Just show up.

If your kids are the age where Halloween is still a full production, this is a solid warm-up to the main event Thursday night.
scoring_notes: Strong geographic fit — Sewell Mill Library is directly in East Cobb. Skews toward families with younger kids, which is a subset of this audience. Free and low-effort to attend. Uniqueness is lower since it's a fairly standard library Halloween event, but the proximity and timing lift it for this newsletter.

event_name: Halloween Cocktail Class at ASW Distillery
blurb:
ASW Distillery is running a Halloween cocktail class Sunday afternoon, and if you've ever wanted to actually learn what you're doing behind a bar instead of just guessing, this is a fun way to spend a few hours.

You get your own bar station, a lead mixologist walking you through the process, and three cocktails made from award-winning spirits to show for it. Halloween theme gives it a little extra energy. It's at the Battery, so you're looking at a 30-ish minute drive from East Cobb, but the afternoon timing makes it an easy out-and-back.

Good date option. Good friend-group option. Three cocktails and new skills by 5 PM is a pretty solid Sunday.
scoring_notes: Hands-on experience events play well with East Cobb's educated, higher-income adult audience. Halloween theming adds seasonal relevance. The Battery location is a slight friction point for East Cobb residents but not a dealbreaker at $118K median income. Skews adult, which fits the empty nester segment well.

event_name: Fifth Annual WE CARE Veterans Fair
blurb:
If you or someone in your family has served, this one is worth putting on the calendar for Thursday. The WE CARE Veterans Fair is a free benefits expo at the Cobb County Civic Center, running all day from 9 AM to 6 PM.

It's built for veterans, active-duty members, National Guard and Reserve, military families, caregivers, and survivors — basically anyone connected to service who wants to know what benefits and resources are actually available to them. East Cobb has a meaningful veteran population, and a lot of people leave benefits on the table simply because they don't know they exist.

This is the fifth year running, which means it's an established event with real resources behind it. Free, local, and genuinely useful. Pass this one along to anyone in your circle who served.
scoring_notes: Annual event rather than a one-night-only, which limits uniqueness. But the civic relevance is high and East Cobb's homeowning, established-family demographic likely includes veterans or military families who would benefit. Free, daytime, and local makes it low-friction to attend. Worth including for community service value.

event_name: Grand Opening: Emily Bourne Grigsby and Athos Menaboni Gallery
blurb:
Kennesaw State is opening a brand new gallery Saturday afternoon, and grand openings are one of those things that only happen once. The Emily Bourne Grigsby and Athos Menaboni Gallery joins KSU's Arts District, and this is your first shot to walk through it before it becomes a regular stop.

Athos Menaboni was a celebrated Georgia artist known for his precise, luminous paintings of birds and nature — his work ended up in the Smithsonian and the White House. Getting a dedicated gallery space near where a lot of you live is genuinely worth noting. Free to attend, no ticket required, and it wraps up in time to make dinner plans.

If you've got a teenager interested in art or a Sunday-afternoon-museum type in the house, bring them along. This is the kind of local thing that's easy to skip and then wish you hadn't.
scoring_notes: Grand openings are by definition one-time events, which lifts the uniqueness score. East Cobb's educated audience skews toward arts appreciation. Menaboni's Georgia legacy gives it local resonance. Free admission removes any friction. Skews toward adults and culture-minded families.

event_name: Murder Mystery Co. Dinner Theater Show
blurb:
Dinner and a show, except you're also a suspect. The Murder Mystery Co. is back at The Hudson Grille in Kennesaw for a Halloween-season whodunit, and if you've never done one of these, this is the right time of year to try it.

You get a three-course meal, a cast of characters who may or may not be the killer, and a room full of strangers who are all trying to crack the case before you do. It's interactive, it's loud, and it's the kind of night that gets genuinely funny once people loosen up. Great for a date night, a group of friends, or honestly any occasion where you want a reason to talk to people you don't know.

Call the box office at 888-659-2952 to book direct and save $9 in fees. Show runs 6:30 to 9:00 PM, which means you're home at a reasonable hour.
scoring_notes: Good adult date-night or group option, close to East Cobb. The Murder Mystery Co. runs monthly events so it's not truly rare, but the Halloween timing adds some seasonal urgency. Dinner included improves the value perception for a $118K median income audience. Skews adult, which works for this newsletter's mix.

blurb:
Multi-Grammy Award-winning guitarist Clay Ross is bringing the American Patchwork Quartet to the Roswell Cultural Arts Center Friday night, and this one is worth clearing your calendar for.

The ensemble pulls from American folk, jazz, country, West African, and East Asian traditions and weaves them into something that genuinely doesn't sound like anything else. Their debut album landed a Grammy nomination. That's not marketing copy — that's a peer vote from the music industry saying this is the real deal.

It's part of Roswell's American Mosaic Series, which means the programming is thoughtful and the crowd tends to be too. A short drive from East Cobb, good music, and the kind of night out that actually gives you something to talk about afterward. Check Roswell365.com for show times and tickets.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for East Cobb's educated, higher-income, 42-median-age audience. This crowd appreciates live music with cultural depth. Grammy-nominated act elevates the uniqueness score. Proximity to East Cobb makes it a natural pick. Skews adult, which works well for the empty nester portion of the audience.

blurb:
This is not your standard haunted house. The William Root House is going full Victorian death-ritual mode for one night, and honestly, it's one of the more fascinating things happening in Cobb County this Halloween season.

After hours, the rooms go dark and fill up with 19th century embalming equipment, mourning jewelry made from actual human hair, a real death mask, and other artifacts from an era when grief was elaborate, public, and deeply ritualized. You tour it yourself, flashlight in hand, at whatever pace you want. It's eerie without being a jump-scare cheap shot.

If you've got a teenager who thinks Halloween is over once the candy runs out, bring them. If you and your partner are looking for something genuinely different to do on a Friday night, this is it. Arrive no later than 8:30 PM to make sure you get the full experience.
scoring_notes: One-night Halloween event with real historical substance. Skews toward curious adults and older teens, which fits East Cobb's mix of empty nesters and families with teen kids well. Uniqueness is high — Victorian mourning artifacts in a darkened historic house is genuinely rare. Price point is unknown but likely accessible given the venue.
